notes: Toolchain 1.1 for Windows x64 (Phase 5H). The exact component set of Toolchain 1.0 for Windows (same official upstream archives, same pins: GHDL 6.0.0 mcode UCRT64 zip; the Apio 1.6.0 bundle; the Apio package set Apio 1.6.0 installs on windows-amd64 with openXC7 2026-09-24 and its xc7a100tcsg324 chipdb), with the compliance changes already made for macOS Toolchain 1.1, each re-checked against the actual Windows contents: (1) the VHDL-87/93 IEEE libraries (they contain the IEEE 1076.3-1995 numeric_bit/numeric_std sources, distributable only unchanged and not for profit) are removed from the GHDL library; (2) the VITAL-95, VITAL-2000 and UPF packages (licence not established) are removed and the GHDL 2008/2019 IEEE library indexes regenerated by GHDL itself with the upstream rules of libraries/Makefile.inc minus those packages; (3) the 111 openFPGALoader bridge bitstreams (no provenance) are removed from the oss-cad-suite package: nothing on Windows programs the Nexys A7 with openFPGALoader (the programmer is Digilent djtgcfg) and the bitstreams are only used by its flash path; (3b) the GHDL plugin-development headers vpi_user.h, synth_gates.h and synth.h (no licence statement; unused at run time) are removed; (4) the licence texts of the bundled native libraries (Fedora MinGW packages, static libraries, Microsoft redistributables) are carried inside the toolchain in licenses/compliance/. MIX-FPGA runs GHDL with --std=08 only. Everything else is byte-identical to Toolchain 1.0.

environment.notes: Every bundled tool runs with PATH = the bundle shims + the operating-system folders only (no developer or student tools), inherited APIO_* and PYTHON* variables removed, and Python bytecode writing disabled so the immutable bundle is never written to.

shims.reason: openXC7 fasm2frames.cmd/bit2fasm.cmd/xc7pll.cmd run a bare "python" from PATH. In Phases 1-4A this silently resolved to the developer machine's C:Python314python.exe. The shim points it at the CPython 3.11.6 shipped inside the official oss-cad-suite package; fasm2frames output was verified byte-identical (hardware.frames sha256 0c4e6307...) to the validated Python 3.14.3 run.

licenceNotes.title: Yosys, Icarus Verilog, GNU Readline and GNU termcap (Windows)
text: `apio/packages/oss-cad-suite/bin/yosys.exe` (Yosys, ISC licence) and `bin/vvp.exe` (Icarus Verilog runtime, version 14.0) import `lib/libreadline8.dll`, GNU Readline 8.2 (GPL-3.0-or-later), which in turn imports `lib/libtermcap-0.dll`, GNU termcap 1.3.1 (GPL-2.0-or-later). `lib/libhistory8.dll` (GNU Readline's history library) ships beside it; no program of the toolchain imports it. These DLLs are the Fedora mingw64 packages `mingw64-readline` 8.2-3.fc39 and `mingw64-termcap` 1.3.1-34.fc39 of the build image YosysHQ uses for its Windows release (`yosyshq/cross-windows-x64:2.3`); each file is identified by the SHA-256 in the package's RPM header (compliance manifest, library group `ocs-fedora-readline` and `ocs-fedora-termcap`). The import tables of all 571 Windows program and library files of this toolchain were read: no other file imports Readline or termcap. In particular `yosys-abc.exe` and `yosys-filterlib.exe` do not load Readline, and the Python 3.11.6 of this package has no `readline` extension module.

MIX-FPGA distributes each program that loads Readline together with it under the terms of the GNU General Public License version 3 (`licenses/GPL-3.0.txt`), with the complete Corresponding Source of both and the build recipe in the source package; GPL-2.0-or-later termcap and the GPL-2.0-or-later Icarus Verilog (every Icarus-authored file of the pinned source grants "either version 2 of the License, or (at your option) any later version") combine with GPLv3 Readline under GPL version 3. Yosys' own licence is in `licenses/yosys-COPYING.txt`. Readline and termcap stay separate DLL files that you can replace.

Yosys 0.63+173 (commit `66306a8ca34cb1dcdafe12a5838fa8f0c1a7f4c2`, with its `abc` and `cxxopts` submodules) reports `git sha1 66306a8ca-dirty`: the YosysHQ build recipe (`oss-cad-suite-build` `ac8c7dba`) edits the compiler name in the tracked `Makefile` before it builds; the recipe, the exact source and the Fedora source packages are in the source package.

licenceNotes.title: Icarus Verilog (Windows)
text: `bin/vvp.exe`, `lib/ivl/ivl.exe`, `ivlpp.exe` and the plugin modules `lib/ivl/*.vpi` are Icarus Verilog (version 14.0, source revision `6767a079560f4528f4beeae82fb33361eb4bc92a`). The Windows build reports `s20251012-140-gf5a178d47-dirty`: the YosysHQ recipe applies a local revert of upstream commit `964878382d3fa77285b73d4657be5bbf95a9aacd` (it changes only `Makefile.in` and `vvp/Makefile.in`) as a new local commit before building, so the hash after `-g` is the hash of that local commit in the build image and differs between builds (the macOS build of the same recipe reports another hash); the exact source and the recipe are in the source package. MIX-FPGA does not run these programs; they are part of the Apio OSS CAD Suite package.

licenceNotes.title: Apio, openXC7 and the other programs of the packages
text: Apio 1.6.0 is GPL-3.0-or-later (`apio/bin/LICENSE`) and the Apio definitions are GPL-3.0-only; the Python 3.14.7 runtime inside the Apio bundle is under the PSF License 2.0. The Apio packages `drivers` (Zadig, libwdi, serial installer) and `graphviz` are NOT redistributed: their folders contain only a placeholder note, and MIX-FPGA never installs or changes a USB driver. The remaining programs of the OSS CAD Suite and openXC7 packages keep the licence texts their suppliers ship (`apio/packages/oss-cad-suite/license/`, one `LICENSE.<tool>` per tool) and the texts in `licenses/compliance/`; MIT, BSD, ISC and Apache-2.0 material retains its notices.

GHDL is GPL-2.0-or-later; its GRT runtime and std.textio are GPLv2, so a program that GHDL generates needs the VHDL sources it was made from. MIX-FPGA runs GHDL in memory (mcode) and distributes no student executables. Qt, GTK, GLib, Pango, Cairo and the other LGPL libraries are separate files used by other programs of the package (for example GTKWave), not by MIX-FPGA; the MPL-2.0 components (Eigen compiled into `nextpnr-xilinx`, the Python package `certifi`) are unmodified and their source is in the source package.

placeholder.reason: Apio 1.6.0 requires a "drivers" package on windows-amd64 (apio/resources/packages.jsonc, restricted-to-platforms) before it runs any command, but only "apio drivers ..." uses it and NexysVHDL never runs that: NexysVHDL installs no USB drivers (Windows programming uses the official Digilent Adept support).
evidence: apio/resources/packages.jsonc at Apio 9fbb279c: drivers restricted to windows-amd64, env adds %p/bin to PATH only.

PE import scan of all 655 PE files of Toolchain 1.0 (scripts/compliance/pe-imports.mjs): no file outside the package imports a DLL that only the drivers package provides (it provides none used elsewhere).
Installed-VSIX process traces (Phase 4B standard and hostile paths, and this phase): zadig, lsusb, lsftdi, ftdi_eeprom and serial_install never run.

serial_install.exe is PJRC's "Serial Installer" for Teensy ((C) 2014 PJRC.COM, LLC; http://www.pjrc.com/teensy/; Comodo code-signed), committed as a prebuilt binary to FPGAwars/tools-drivers (package/bin, first commit 2025-06-09) with no license file.
Experiment: Apio 1.6.0 with an empty drivers folder and a matching installed_packages.json entry reports "All Apio packages are installed OK" and runs with all network access blocked.
